race_name: Nordic Chase Berlin to Copenhagen Road

top_categories.workout_context: 441 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
At Nordic Chase Berlin to Copenhagen Road, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Nordic Chase Berlin to Copenhagen Road's lowland point-to-point road ultra rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
441 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
8,760ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.

Road-specific control matters at Nordic Chase Berlin to Copenhagen Road. Practice on lowland point-to-point road ultra: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 441 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Nordic Chase Berlin to Copenhagen Road's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before race day.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 441 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 8,760ft of climbing on lowland point-to-point road ultra does to your power file on race day.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Nordic Chase Berlin to Copenhagen Road. Train it until it feels boring.
8,760ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
Low-cadence force work supports 8,760ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 441 miles: 80–100g carbs/hour from mile 1 — don’t wait until you’re hungry. Practice your exact race-day nutrition in every long training ride. Carry backup calories. 441 miles burns 8,000–12,000+ calories — you cannot replace them all, but you must try.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Nordic Chase Berlin to Copenhagen Road rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on lowland point-to-point road ultra to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Over Under, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 441 miles of lowland point-to-point road ultra in Berlin, Germany to Copenhagen, Denmark.
